faqs.q: Do I need a card for a tour or a pass?
faqs.a: No. Tours and the 3-day pass are free. We do not ask for a card.

faqs.q: What should I bring on my first visit?
faqs.a: Photo ID, if you want a 3-day pass. Wear what you move in. Bring a water bottle. We have towels for Summit members.

faqs.q: I am new or coming back from an injury. Where do I start?
faqs.a: Book a tour and tell us. We match you with a coach and an easy class. Many members start with Mobility 30 or Aqua Fit.
No. Memberships are month to month.

faqs.q: How do I cancel or freeze?
faqs.a: Give 30 days' notice in the app or at the desk. A freeze costs $10 a month for 1 to 3 months.

faqs.q: What fees are there besides the monthly price?
faqs.a: Enrollment is $0 during Fall climb (otherwise $49). A $49 annual facility fee is charged in March.
Book up to 7 days ahead (Summit: 9). Cancel free up to 2 hours before. Later is a late cancel. Three late cancels in 30 days pause booking for 3 days. Waitlists move up until 1 hour before class.

faqs.q: What ages can use kids club?
faqs.a: Ages 6 months to 12 years, in 2-hour blocks. A parent checks in at the same club and stays in the building.

Yes. Teens 13 to 17 can book classes marked Teen OK, such as Teen Strength. A parent signs the waiver and manages billing. Strength floor use without a coach starts at age 16. Sauna and cold plunge are for ages 18 and up.

faqs.q: Is there an age limit for members?
faqs.a: Adults of any age can join. We have easy classes, a warm-water pool and coaches who work with older members.

homeFaq.q: Do I need a card for a tour or a pass?
homeFaq.a: No. Tours and the 3-day pass are free and need no card.
No. Memberships are month to month. Cancel or freeze with 30 days' notice.

homeFaq.q: Can I use more than one club?
homeFaq.a: Ridge and Summit work at all 5 clubs. Trailhead works at your home club.

homeFaq.q: Is there something for my kids?
homeFaq.a: Yes. Kids club at Mesa – Dobson, Mesa – Red Mountain and Gilbert – Val Vista.

homeFaq.a: Book a tour and tell us. We will match you with a coach and an easy class.

journal.title: Your first Climb Cycle: five things to know
journal.dek: Heavy load, short hills and a coach calling the numbers. Here is how to get through your first 45 minutes.
journal.author: marisol-vega
journal.caption: Cycle studio at Val Vista, riders mid-climb, 6 a.m.
sections: Arrive early
Show up 10 minutes before class. A coach sets your seat and handlebars. Ask for the set-up, even if you think you know it. A bike that fits makes the hour easier.
Pick a load you can talk over
The coach calls out loads from 1 to 10. Start at 3 or 4. You can always add. You cannot easily take away halfway up a hill.
Stand when you are told, not before
Standing climbs are short. Sit when your legs say sit. Nobody is watching your cadence.
Drink early
It is Arizona. Water before class, a sip every few minutes, and more after.
Come back on Thursday
The second class is easier than the first. The third is where it starts to feel like yours.

journal.title: A first week back after surgery
journal.dek: What a coach looks for, what to skip, and why the warm pool is a good first stop.
journal.author: imani-brooks
journal.caption: Warm-water pool at Dobson, a member and a coach
sections: Ask your surgeon first
Get a clear yes, and ask what to avoid. Bring the notes to your tour. A coach can read a surgeon's note and turn it into a first week.
Start in the warm pool
The Dobson therapy pool stays at 90 to 92°F. The water holds your weight, so a sore knee or hip can move without load. Ten easy minutes is a good first day.
Pick Mobility 30, not a hard class
Thirty minutes of joint prep at intensity 1. You choose the range. Nobody needs you to touch your toes.
Keep a short log
Write one line a day: what you did, how it felt the next morning. Your coach reads it before the second session.
Add one thing a week
A second class, a longer swim, a little load. If a week feels like too much, repeat it. That is allowed.

journal.title: What to eat before a 6:00 a.m. class
journal.dek: A banana, some salt, and water. A short guide for people who do not wake up hungry.
journal.author: nadia-kowalski
journal.caption: Café counter at Dobson, early morning
sections: If you can eat, eat small
Half a banana or a slice of toast, 30 to 45 minutes before class. Skip anything heavy or fried.
If you cannot, drink
A glass of water and a pinch of salt is enough for a 45-minute class. Your body has fuel for it.
Coffee is fine
One cup is fine. Two on an empty stomach and a hard interval class is a bad mix.
Eat after
Within an hour, add protein and something with carbohydrate. Eggs and fruit. Yogurt and oats. The Dobson café opens at 6:00 a.m.
Watch the heat
From June to September, add a second glass of water to your morning. Sweat in a dry climate disappears fast.

journal.title: Packing for kids club, in 5 minutes
journal.dek: Socks, a water bottle and a note about allergies. Here is the rest.
journal.author: luis-ortega
journal.caption: Kids club check-in door, Val Vista
sections: Socks and a water bottle
Children play barefoot or in socks. Label the bottle. We refill it.
One change of clothes
Spills and splash pad days happen. A small bag with a dry set saves a bad evening.
Tell us about allergies
Add allergy and medical notes in the app before you arrive. The staff read them at check-in.
Check in at the same club
Kids club blocks are 2 hours, and you stay in the building. An unclaimed block is released 15 minutes after it starts.
Plan your own two hours
Book a class that fits inside the block, with time to shower. Most parents pick a 45-minute class and a swim.

journal.title: The Heritage rooftop deck is open to all members
journal.dek: Mobility sessions at golden hour, Tuesday to Saturday.
journal.author: devon-hart
journal.caption: Rooftop mobility deck at golden hour
sections: What opened
The rooftop mobility deck at Gilbert – Heritage is open to every member, not only Summit. Mats, bands and foam rollers are up there.
When to go
Mobility 30 runs at golden hour, Tuesday to Saturday. In October the light is soft from about 5:30 p.m.
What to bring
Water and a layer. The deck is in the open air and it cools quickly after the sun drops.
Access
A lift and stairs reach the deck. Both are step-free from the lobby.
Rules
No lifting on the deck. Phones stay in your pocket during class. The deck closes at 8:00 p.m.

journal.title: Pickleball in the heat: a short guide
journal.dek: Play early, drink before you are thirsty, and use the shade sails.
journal.author: ray-delgado
journal.caption: Red Mountain courts at 6:30 a.m.
sections: Play before 9:00 a.m.
From June to September the courts are comfortable before 9:00 a.m. and hard work after 11:00. Book the early slot.
Drink before you are thirsty
A cup of water every two games. By the time you are thirsty you are already behind.
Use the shade
Red Mountain's courts have shade at the north end after 7:30 a.m. Swap ends so nobody plays in the sun all game.
Dress for it
Light colors, a hat between points, and sunscreen on your ears. Bring a spare shirt for the end of a long session.
Know when to stop
Dizziness, a headache or cramps mean sit down and drink. Tell the desk. The recovery lounge is a good place to cool off.
